t: A Romanian principality founded in the mid-14th century between the Carpathians and the Dniester, independent of Hungary from about 1359.
Stephen the Great defeated the Ottomans at Vaslui in 1475, but Moldavia became an Ottoman tributary and was ruled by Phanariots 1711–1821.
It lost Bukovina to Austria and Bessarabia to Russia, and in 1859 united with Wallachia to form Romania.
dyk: The Ottomans called Moldavia Kara Boğdan, “Black Bogdania”, after its founding prince Bogdan I, and the name survived in Turkish for centuries.
